subject: Procurement follow-up: Redwood vendor setup & payment method
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Redwood procurement intake & next steps

Hi Lena —

Great to meet earlier today. Thanks for walking through Acme's use case and traffic profile; the team is excited about running inference on Redwood Dedicated for your in-house analytics pipelines. Quick recap + next steps so procurement has what it needs: 

- Proposed commercial path: start Hosted/API for beta (card) then transition to Reserved/Dedicated with PO for production.
- Procurement items likely needed: vendor setup packet, W-9, banking details, standard SOW/Order Form + PO process.
- Marketplace: you mentioned potential interest in using our AWS Marketplace listing for consolidated billing — let us know if procurement prefers marketplace invoices.

Action items:
1) I’ll send our vendor setup packet and W-9.
2) Can procurement confirm whether payments will be PO (net 30) or card for the initial pilot?
3) If PO, please share vendor portal instructions or the required internal form.

I’ve looped in Monica from Sales Ops and Dylan (solutions) to help with the vendor packet and technical onboarding.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Attachments: vendor_setup_packet.pdf (vendor packet, includes instructions), W-9_Redwood.pdf

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood procurement intake & next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the summary — very helpful. Quick answers from our side: 

- For the pilot, finance prefers to pay by credit card to avoid setting up a PO immediately.
- For production, we'll need PO-based invoicing (Net 30).
- Procurement will need your vendor setup packet and a completed internal "vendor onboarding" form (I've attached the PDF in my reply). Also need Redwood's banking details for ACH and a W-9.

Two questions:
1) Do you have a dedicated vendor record in AWS Marketplace? If so, do you support consolidated marketplace billing for enterprise customers?
2) Are there any compliance docs we should start collecting (SOC 2 evidence, data processing addendum)?

Looping in procurement so they can attach the internal vendor onboarding form.

Best,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Product 
Acme Analytics
lena.ortiz@acme-analytics.com

Attachment: Acme_VendorOnboarding_Form.pdf (filled by Acme)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-analytics.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood procurement intake & next steps

Hi Lena / Procurement —

Thanks — I attached the vendor setup packet and our W-9 (both PDFs). The packet includes:
- Redwood vendor information sheet (legal name, remit-to address)
- Banking details for ACH payments (bank name, ACH routing, account number)
- Standard payment terms (Net 30 for PO customers; card accepted for pilots)
- Instructions for registering on our vendor portal and the AWS Marketplace vendor guidance.

On your questions:
- AWS Marketplace: yes, we are listed and can enable consolidated marketplace billing for enterprise accounts — this is handled as an optional procurement path. If you want marketplace invoices, procurement should flag that during vendor setup and we can route billing accordingly.
- Compliance: I’ve included links to our SOC 2 summary and standard DPA in the packet. If you need the full SOC 2 report or additional attestations, follow-up with monica_patel@redwood.com and she'll coordinate an NDA/controlled-sharing flow.

Next steps from Redwood:
1) Please return your internal vendor onboarding form and confirm PO vs card for the production rollout (we noted pilot = card).
2) If PO, we’ll generate an Order Form to sign (DocuSign link) and confirm net terms.
3) If you want marketplace billing, tell us now so we can include marketplace onboarding in the vendor packet.

Doc links: https://app.redwood.com/vendor-portal/setup/RDW-ACME-2491
DocuSign (order form draft): https://docusign.net/Redwood_ACME_vendorsetup

Thanks —
Marissa

Attachments: vendor_setup_packet.pdf, W-9_Redwood.pdf, redwood_vendor_portal_instructions.pdf

From: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Redwood procurement intake & next steps

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the packet. We reviewed internally and can confirm the following: 

- Pilot payment: credit card (confirmed).
- Production: PO with Net 30 terms; please send the Order Form for signature.
- Attached our completed internal vendor onboarding form and bank/vendor approval checklist.

Request from procurement:
1) Please confirm the exact remit-to address and the ACH details as shown in your vendor packet (we need to copy into our AP system).
2) We will need a completed W-9 with a dated signature for our file; the W-9 you sent is acceptable but can you confirm the date signed?
3) We prefer to use AWS Marketplace only if your team can guarantee consolidated invoice visibility for our billing admin — can Monica confirm if that is straightforward?

Once we have the signed Order Form and the final W-9 date, we can issue a PO and kick off onboarding.

Thanks —
Acme Procurement
procurement@acme-analytics.com

Attachment: Acme_Completed_VendorOnboarding_Form.pdf, Acme_AP_Checklist.xlsx
